picks.why: Egerszalók estate in the Bükk foothills whose range is built around Bikavér; Merengő, its Bikavér Superior, is the deeper, firmer tier of the blend that gives Eger its name.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year and the house's history from two sources, and Merengő's blend in words; the Hangács and Nagy-Eged Grand Superior site wines belong among the others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Noszvaj family house, a long standing name for Bikavér; its Grand Superior from the southern slopes of Nagy-Eged teaches the highest tier of the Eger blend and the hill that gives its most structured wine.
picks.note: Teach the Grand Superior of the Nagy-Eged dűlő, from vines planted in 2008 by the house's account: confirm the label words and the blend in words. The house's Vili Papa cuvée carries a living founder's name, so it is not taught. Give the founding year only from two sources.

picks.why: Eger estate that keeps its late founder's name and is known in the district's premium tier for Bikavér and Kékfrankos; its Egri Bikavér is the wine of the house to know.
picks.note: Confirm from two sources the founder's career in Tuscany (Ornellaia in Bolgheri, from memory and unconfirmed here), his dates and his death, said to be in 2005. A living heir shares the founder's name, so give the founder his dates or describe him. Confirm the founding year and the Bikavér's label.

picks.why: Eger estate made in an abandoned stone quarry on the edge of the town by a first generation winemaker; its Egri Bikavér is the classic tier of the blend, the wine the region record knows the house for.
picks.note: Founded in 1998 by one account: confirm from a second source, with the quarry's story. The house's varietal Kékfrankos and its other cuvées belong among the others. Name no living person.

picks.why: Eger estate named for a historic count, with vines on the Nagy-Eged hill; its Bikavér Superior from that hill shows the limestone side of the blend.
picks.note: Founded in 1999 by one account: confirm. Confirm the label words (Nagy-Eged on the label, Superior or Grand Superior in the years taught), and tell the count it is named for only with his dates from two sources. The house's Kadarka Superior is for the others.

picks.why: Gyöngyös family cellar given chiefly to white wine; its Sárhegy Olaszrizling, from the Sár-hegy by the town, is the district's lead white grape from a named hill.
picks.note: Sources disagree on the founding (1904 and 1906 both given): leave the year empty unless two agree. Confirm the Sárhegy bottling's label and the hill's soil.

picks.why: Gyöngyöstarján family cellar of the third generation; its Kékfrankos speaks for the Mátra as a new home of the grape, beside the old vine, barrel aged Hárslevelű it also makes.
picks.note: Teach the bottling the house leads with, the Kékfrankos or the old vine Hárslevelű; if it is the Hárslevelű, the wine is renamed with the checker's agreement. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small Gyöngyöspata family estate, begun on Olaszrizling in 2004 and made with a natural hand; its Hárslevelű shows the house beyond the district's carafe whites.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: the sources read show a Hárslevelű at a tasting of the grape and the house begun on Olaszrizling, and name no flagship. Confirm the wine the house leads with, its label and the 2004 start from a second source, else propose a swap. The house carries a living name, so the prose says the family.

picks.why: Nagyréde family cellar of 1999, Bárdos and Son by its name; its Irsai Olivér is the district's light, aromatic spring wine, drunk within the year.
picks.note: Founded in 1999 by the house's own history: confirm with a second source, and confirm that the Irsai Olivér is the wine it leads with. Szőke Mátyás is given the same grape: one of the two may take another wine.

picks.why: Gyöngyöstarján family cellar of the village of family estates on loess over andesite; its Irsai Olivér is the Mátra's spring white, light and aromatic.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: a directory names only an Irsai Olivér and a Merlot. Confirm the wine the house leads with, its label and its history from two sources, else propose a swap; the house carries a living name, so the prose says the family.

picks.why: Balf estate of a family that also farms across the border in Burgenland; its Kékfrankos from the Steiner vineyard, where grey slate reaches the surface, is the district's single vineyard Kékfrankos to know.
picks.note: Confirm the vineyard's name on the label (Steiner or Spern Steiner) and its soil. The family's Austrian estate is not in wave one's Burgenland group, and Sopron is its Hungarian home. Give the year the family came to Balf only from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Sopron family estate on the hills above the town whose Kékfrankos show the schist side of the district; Újra Együtt, Together Again, is one of the two Kékfrankos it is known for.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: one account gives the house a lighter, juicier Kékfrankos, Újra Együtt, and a more complex one with tannic grip. Confirm both names, what the name means for the family, and teach the one the house leads with; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Sopron house of wine and sparkling wine founded in 1997, whose traditional method Chardonnay Brut shows the district beyond its peppery reds.
picks.note: Confirm 1997 and the method from the house or a second source, and the time on lees in words; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small family winery in the hills between Fertőrákos and Balf, taken over by a daughter of the family after her father's death; its Pinot Noir shows the light, red fruited side of the lakeside climate.
picks.note: The house also makes Kékfrankos, one of them from the Steiner vineyard: confirm whether the Pinot Noir or a Kékfrankos is the wine to teach, and the founding year (2002 by one listing, which another account contradicts). Name no living person.

picks.why: Fertőrákos estate on the lake shore, a chef's winery in the family farmhouse on the village's main street; its Kékfrankos from a bare, chalky vineyard of the village is the wine to know.
picks.note: Confirm the Kékfrankos's label and site name and whether a sweet wine or another red leads, as the region record says the house makes both; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Badacsony estate that brought Kéknyelű back from near extinction in the 1990s; its Kéknyelű is the hill's rare native white, lean, mineral and slow to open.
picks.note: The revival is the region record's claim: confirm it and the founding year from two sources, and the label words (Badacsonyi Kéknyelű). Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Badacsony family estate with vineyards on several witness hills of the lake; its Szürkebarát teaches the hill's historic white, Pinot Gris grown on basalt.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: the house grows Olaszrizling, Rajnai Rizling, Szürkebarát, Kéknyelű and Furmint, and the sources read name no flagship. Confirm a Szürkebarát under the house's name, else rename the wine to the one it leads with.

picks.why: Badacsony estate of Swedish founders given to Rajnai Rizling, the true Riesling, for which it makes the case on basalt.
picks.note: Confirm the founding year and the founders' story from two sources and the label words; name no living person.

picks.why: Estate at the foot of Csobánc on the northern shore whose basalt grown Olaszrizling shows the structure of the witness hills, against the sandstone Olaszrizling of Csopak.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: the sources read list a Csobánc wine and a Rajnai Rizling from the Kápolna-domb site but name no flagship. Confirm the house's leading bottling and its label; if it is the Riesling, a swap is needed against Villa Sandahl's.

picks.why: Csopak family house on an estate that once belonged to a bishop of Veszprém, whose Olaszrizling helped set the village's charter style; Lőczedombi is its single vineyard Olaszrizling of old vines on Permian sandstone.
picks.note: The family there since 1998 by one account and the bishop's estate (the Ranolder White cuvée is named for him): confirm both, the bishop's dates and the charter story from two sources. Ranolder White, an Olaszrizling and Furmint cuvée, belongs among the others.

picks.why: Somló estate that put traditional method sparkling wine built on Furmint on the hill's map beside its still Juhfark; Prestige Brut is its sparkling wine to know.
picks.note: Confirm from two sources that Prestige Brut is Furmint led, its time on lees in words and the founding year; the house's Juhfark, whole cluster pressed and partly fermented in oak, is for the others.

picks.why: Somlóvásárhely house whose founder, once head of the state co-operative, bottled the first privately made Somló wines in 1982; its single vineyard Juhfark from the Grófi vineyard is the hill's grape from a named site.
picks.note: Teach the single vineyard Juhfark of the Grófi dűlő and confirm its label words. Confirm 1982 and the co-operative story from a second source; the founder is dead, so name him only with his dates from two sources.

picks.why: Small Somló family cellar in the old manner, with long cask ageing and wines that need years; its Juhfark is the sheep's tail grape in the style the hill was known for.
picks.note: Confirm the cellar's ageing and the founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Somló cellar of a winemaker of the hill's revival after communism, which made white wine alone; its Juhfark is the wine to know.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: confirm whether Juhfark or Hárslevelű is the house's leading wine, the house's name on the label, and when the founder retired and to whom the cellar passed, as history with its year. The founder may be living: describe him, never name him.

picks.why: The abbey cellar tied to the Benedictines of Pannonhalma, a reminder that the church shaped Somló's vineyards for centuries; its Juhfark is the hill's own grape.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: the sources read show the cellar only at a Juhfark tasting. Confirm its tie to Pannonhalma, its history and the wine it leads with from two sources, else propose a swap.

picks.why: Szekszárd family estate that made the case for Kadarka and Kékfrankos as the district's own voice; Barbár, its flagship blend, is a bigger, more intense cousin of Bikavér among the district's named blends.
picks.note: Confirm Barbár's grapes in words and how the house describes it, and the family's history in the district from two sources; the Kadarka is for the others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Large modern Szekszárd family estate whose ripe Bordeaux variety reds carried the district's name abroad in the 2000s; Regnum, a blend led by Merlot and Cabernet Franc, is the wine to know.
picks.note: Confirm Regnum's grapes in words and the house's founding from two sources (one article marks a twentieth anniversary); Primarius Merlot and the Gurovica Kékfrankos belong among the others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Szekszárd family house working old Kadarka plantings; Nagyapám, My Grandfather, is its Kadarka from the estate's own selections of old vines, the bottle to pour when a guest asks what the native grape tastes like.
picks.note: Confirm the clone selection story, the family's history and the label words from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Szekszárd family estate of two generations whose single vineyard Bikavér and Kékfrankos show the valley sites; Valles, its Prémium Bikavér, is led by Kékfrankos with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and a little Kadarka.
picks.note: The label reads Valles with Szekszárdi Bikavér and Prémium in one order or another: confirm the words and the blend in words, and the family's history. The house carries a living name, so the prose says the family.

picks.why: Traditional Szekszárd house with cellars in the old lanes of the town, known for Bikavér and Kadarka; its single vineyard Kékfrankos from the Porkoláb valley shows the district's premium Kékfrankos.
picks.note: Confirm the label words (Porkoláb or Porkoláb-völgy, with Kékfrankos), the house's history and founding from two sources, and whether its Bikavér is the wine it leads with; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Villány family house whose Kopar cuvée and varietal Cabernet Franc gave the district its modern reputation; Kopar, its flagship, is a blend named for the stony limestone slope of that name above the town.
picks.note: The house is the Gere Attila winery, not the separate Gere Tamás and Zsolt winery; name no living member of the family. Confirm Kopar's grapes in words, its first vintage (a twentieth vintage in 2021 by one account) and that the name is the Kopár site's.

picks.why: One of the district's founding modern estates, with cellars under the town; Capella is the house's own selection, a Villány red blend made only in exceptional years.
picks.note: Confirm Capella's grapes in words, the years it is made and the house's history from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Estate at Kisharsány under Szársomlyó, known for varietal reds and a willingness to experiment; Duennium, its flagship cuvée, is made only in the vintages the house judges fit.
picks.note: Kisharsány is the region record's: confirm it, the founding year and Duennium's grapes in words from two sources.

picks.why: Modern Villány estate with a sister cellar in Tokaj; Cuvée 7, its flagship, is a blend led by Cabernet Sauvignon from the Kopár, Konkoly and Ördögárok vineyards.
picks.note: Confirm the blend in words and the founding year from two sources; the Tokaj cellar is not in wave one's Tokaj group. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Villány estate of 1997, farmed organically since 2009 and led by Cabernet Franc; its Kúria Cabernet Franc is the grape the district gave its own designation, Villányi Franc.
picks.note: Teach the Kúria Cabernet Franc and confirm its label words and whether it carries Villányi Franc; confirm 1997 and the organic farming from 2009 from the estate or a second source. The house carries a living name, so the prose says the founder.

picks.why: Soltvadkert family house that built its modern winery in 1987 on a long family history of vineyards on the plain; its Cserszegi Fűszeres is the aromatic white that is the house's calling card.
picks.note: Confirm 1987 from a second source and the house's name on the label (Frittmann or Frittmann Testvérek); its Irsai Olivér and rosé belong among the others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Kiskőrös family estate of three generations on the sand; Néró, the red grape it makes as a rosé, a red and a traditional siller, is its flagship, the barrel fermented rosé the bottling it is known for.
picks.note: Choose the Néró bottling the house leads with (the barrel fermented rosé by one account) and confirm the grape's parentage before writing it; the region record's old vine Kadarka and Kékfrankos are not borne out by the sources read.

picks.why: Soltvadkert estate with a wide range of aromatic whites and soft reds, a picture of what the plain does well; its Kunsági Kékfrankos Rosé is the dry, pale rosé of the sand.
picks.note: Pick in doubt on the wine: the only bottling found is a Kunsági Kékfrankos Rosé sold widely at home. Confirm the wine the house leads with (an aromatic white may be truer) and its history from two sources.

picks.why: Family estate of Szigetcsép on the Danube's Csepel island, making wine since 1994 and one of the True Kunság cellars; its rosé of Kékfrankos, Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir is the wine the family is known for.
picks.note: Confirm that Szigetcsép lies within the Kunság district, the label words and the blend in words. Not the Gál Tibor estate of Eger, nor the Gál wineries of Villány. Name no living member of the family.
